title: Federation middleware runs current_authority() synchronously on async workers for binding and executor routes (blocks runtime threads during StateInner holds)
outcome: Found by Opus3 (TermAl mailbox 03723eab #5765). ensure_current, which is current_authority() taking the link mutex and then StateInner (federation_channel_authority.rs:28-36), runs synchronously on the ASYNC worker in the authenticated middleware, both before the handler (federation_http_authenticate.rs:170) and after it (:227), outside any timeout. Only the prompt-policy route runs these checks on the blocking pool (:159, :217). During a multi-second StateInner hold, every authenticated request blocks an async runtime worker twice and its deadline cannot fire. w-3bddbf73af2a moves the relay and mailbox routes onto the blocking pool under the deadline. This item covers the remaining durable routes, binding and executor, with the same pattern: same checks, same order.
acceptance: The binding and executor routes run their pre- and post-handler authority checks on the blocking pool under the request deadline, with the same checks and order. A behaviour test shows that a StateInner hold during such a request does not block an async worker and that the deadline outcome is still produced, with no wall-clock thresholds.
The review pair is clean, and the full gate passes on the exact landed input.
